_note: Sixteen directions, each an argument about how a food business should look, not a colour scheme. A direction is dealt for a job and may be pinned for a brand; the operator can always choose another. `posture` is what the brand interview maps an answer to.

directions.name: The quiet ledger
directions.idea: A broadsheet for a business that keeps books: one measured line, a hairline, a specimen of the record. Trust comes from restraint, not from a badge.
rules: one hairline under the header and one under the footer, never both around a block
the headline is the only large element; everything else is 3 mm of quiet
numbers are set in the label face so they read as evidence

directions.name: Field notes
directions.idea: A field guide page: a place, a date, a crop, a note in the margin. The design says the work happens outside and is written down.
rules: a photograph is a band across the top, never a background for type
the date belongs on the card, in the label face
leave the top-left corner empty so the eye starts on the headline

directions.name: The pantry shelf
directions.idea: The metaphor made physical: jars on a shelf, a handwritten label, a receipt. Warmth without nostalgia for its own sake.
rules: the mono label is the handwriting stand-in — tracked, small, never a script font
one warm rule, no boxes
stack the list left and keep the right margin empty

directions.name: One long table
directions.idea: Dark, communal, mission-led. A plate set for one, and a belief about who the food is for.
rules: dark ground, cream type, one green or wheat accent
no boxes, no badges, no gradient
allow a long serif line to breathe; do not fill the empty right half

directions.name: The workbench
directions.idea: Product-first proof: a real number, a real date, a real record. The card behaves like the label on a crate.
rules: the label face carries the facts; the grotesque carries the claim
align every fact to one left edge
a rule is a separator, not decoration

directions.name: Bread & ledger
directions.idea: Poster campaign: four words, enormous, in a condensed face. The message lands before the explanation.
rules: the display size is the idea; do not shrink it to fit more words
one accent only, and only on a rule or a single line
if the words do not fit at poster size, the words are wrong

directions.name: Market chalk
directions.idea: The board at the stall: tall capitals, a price, a line drawn by hand that is not a handwriting font.
rules: light type on a dark ground, no chalk texture
prices in the label face, aligned right
leave the bottom third for the day and the place

directions.name: Produce catalogue
directions.idea: A grower's list, set like a catalogue: named varieties, a date, no adjectives. The card is an index, not an advertisement.
rules: variety names are the headline; the category is the eyebrow
one column, generous leading, a hairline between rows
no exclamation marks anywhere on the card

directions.name: Seasonal almanac
directions.idea: A month page: what is coming, what is going, what is only here for a fortnight. Time is the subject.
rules: the month is a tracked label, not a headline
the list is the headline; set it larger than a list normally is
one accent rule under the month

directions.name: Harvest festival
directions.idea: Celebration with a straight face: a big red, a big line, a date. For the one week a year the business shouts.
rules: the accent may be decoration here, but never behind type it cannot carry
one date, one place, one action
do not add a second red

directions.name: The apothecary
directions.idea: Brown glass and small caps: a tincture, a tonic, a cordial. Precision is the aesthetic.
rules: the display face is the mono; the warmth comes from the serif body
tracked capitals for every label
no illustration, no icon, no drop shadow

directions.name: Green grocer
directions.idea: Bright, plain, modern: a shopfront painted last year. Clean type, one accent, produce does the colour.
rules: one family, three weights — hierarchy from weight and size only
the accent is a rule or a single word, never a background wash
left-aligned throughout; nothing centred

directions.name: Bistro menu
directions.idea: A printed menu from a place that has been there a while: a rule, a small caps heading, a price at the right edge.
rules: prices right-aligned to one edge, never mid-row
one rule under the heading, none between dishes
set the whole card in one colour plus the accent

directions.name: Trust & records
directions.idea: The specimen: a certificate number, a batch, a date. For the buyer who needs to check something.
rules: every claim carries its reference on the same line
the mono face is for anything an auditor would read
no certification badges — they belong to the certifier

directions.name: Dawn run
directions.idea: The delivery window as a timetable: a route, a time, a cut-off. Movement rather than produce.
rules: times are the largest thing after the headline
one vertical rhythm for every row
a cut-off is stated once, in the accent

directions.name: Paper bag
directions.idea: Kraft, a stamp, a name typed on a machine. The card looks like the thing the food arrives in.
rules: the label face carries the name and the date
one rule that looks stamped, not drawn
keep at least a third of the card empty
